Capability-matrix long-context retrieval fixture.

This file exists to test whether a delegated local model can retrieve a single
planted fact buried inside a larger body of otherwise irrelevant filler text.
The runner asks only: "what is the value of MAGIC_TOKEN?" The correct answer is
pinned below and must not be changed once runs have started, or the answer key
drifts.

--- filler begins ---

The maintenance window opens on the first Tuesday of each month. Operators are
expected to drain the queue before applying updates, and to confirm that the
dead-letter queue is empty before proceeding. Retries use exponential backoff
with a ceiling of three attempts. Jobs that exhaust their retries are parked for
manual review. None of this is relevant to the question being asked; it is here
only to add distance between the start of the file and the planted value.

The provisioning script reads its configuration from a loopback-only endpoint.
It never exposes the service to the wider network, and it refuses to start if a
non-loopback bind address is supplied. Health checks run every two seconds, and
a lease is considered stale after ten seconds without a heartbeat. Cooldown
after a failed lease is thirty seconds. These numbers are illustrative and are
not the value being sought.

Documentation for the ingestion pipeline describes five stages: intake,
validation, normalization, enrichment, and storage. Each stage emits structured
telemetry. The enrichment stage is the most expensive and is the usual suspect
when latency rises. Engineers are reminded to check the enrichment stage first
before assuming the model server is at fault. This paragraph, too, is filler.

A note on style: prose in this fixture is deliberately bland and repetitive so
that no sentence stands out on surface features alone. A model that simply
echoes the most vivid sentence will fail, because the planted value is stated
plainly and without emphasis, surrounded by equally plain sentences.

MAGIC_TOKEN = "velvet-harbor-3391"

The remainder of the file continues the pattern of unrelated operational notes.
Backups are written nightly and verified weekly. Restores are rehearsed once per
quarter. Access to the backup bucket is limited to two named operators, and all
access is logged. Log retention is ninety days. Again, none of these figures is
the planted value; they are decoys chosen to look plausible.

The scheduler supports both interval and cron-style triggers. Interval triggers
are clamped to a minimum of sixty seconds. Cron triggers are evaluated in the
host's local timezone unless an explicit timezone is supplied. Missed triggers
are not backfilled by default. A configuration flag can enable backfill for a
bounded lookback window, but this is discouraged in production.

Capacity planning assumes a steady-state load with occasional bursts. The system
is sized for the ninety-fifth percentile of historical demand, with headroom for
short spikes. When sustained demand exceeds the provisioned capacity, the queue
depth grows and the oldest jobs are shed according to the configured policy.
Operators receive an alert when queue depth crosses a warning threshold.

This concludes the filler. The only fact a runner should extract from this file
is the value assigned to MAGIC_TOKEN above.
